author: haiku
reason: B opens with the one rule that explains the whole design: A may write only while it holds a lease kept outside A, and the command revokes that lease, waits it out, then promotes B. Its flowchart, trigger table and short sections then make the mechanism quick to grasp, while A covers the same ground with more completeness but buries it under a long glossary, repetition and a sprawling diagram.

author: haiku
reason: B is the better handoff for an engineer new to the project: it starts with a summary of how things run today, defines every term it uses (WAL, epoch, lease, fencer, reaper), and lays out each step with its trigger, data and failure handling. A is tighter and well reasoned, but it assumes the reader already knows the stack and its vocabulary.

author: haiku
reason: A opens with four short points on the design (Postgres holds all state, unique keys coordinate the two instances, timers are job rows, all times come from the database clock), so the whole mechanism is clear before the diagram; B pads the start with definitions a smart engineer does not need, such as webhook and idempotent, and its tick-claim and fencing scheme is harder to follow and admits a gap where a service and rule can stop being evaluated.
